Na seriji MR presjeka desnog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala lateralnog
kolateralnog ligamenata, prednjeg i stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarne
tetive i tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Kompleksna ruptura korpusa i stražnjeg roga medijalnog meniska, s "flap" komponentom koja se
prebacuje iznad stražnjeg roga meniska u području korijena. Korpus meniska periferno je
potisnut.
Lateralni menisk uredne je morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Reaktivni periligamentarni edem uz medijalni kolateralni ligament.
Fisure i defekti pune debljine hrskavice obje fasete patele (hondromalacija 3. stupnja prema
ICRS klasifikaciji),  uz sitne rubne osteofite - OA promjene.
Ostale prikazane artikulacijske hrskavice prožete su plitkim fisurama (hondromalacija 2. stupnja
prema ICRS klasifikaciji), uz sitne rubne osteofite FT zgloba - OA promjene.
Koštani edem medijalnog kondila tibije.
Enhondrom u lateralnom aspektu distalne metafize femura promjera 13 mm.
Opsežan izljev u koljenu, masivna poplitealna (Bakerova) cista uz koju se nalazi subfascijalna
slobodna tekućina uz stražnji rub m. gastroknemijusa. Opisano je suspektno na rupturu
Bakerove ciste, bez potpune drenaže njenog sadržaja.
Varikoziteti potkožnih vena poplitealno.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

Technique: MRI of the knee. ACL normal. MCL normal. Degenerative changes of both meniscus. Incipient MRI signs of chondromalacia of all thre compartments. Prepatelar bursitis. No baker's cyst. No effusion. Conclusion: Chondromalacia of  patelofemoral compartment.

Clinical information: Left knee pain for 8 weeks, atraumatic. No improvement with physiotherapy/rehabilitation. Positive meniscus tests. Concern for LCL tear versus lateral meniscal tear. Rule out internal derangement of the knee.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
There is a radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 4.5 x 3.5 mm. There is an fraying of the residual posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There are no displaced meniscal fragments. There is a moderate mucoid degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is no acute tear of the lateral meniscus.

The cruciate ligaments are intact. There is a moderate thickening with associated T2 hyperintensity of the proximal medial collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial and lateral femorotibial joint compartment. 

There is an mild chondrosis at the medial and lateral patellar facet with focal superficial cartilage irregularities at the lateral patellar facet. There are no cartilage defects, no subchondral bone marrow edema.

There is no joint effusion. There is no Baker's cyst. 

The joint articulations are well-maintained. 

There is a lobulated ganglion cyst extending along the popliteus tendon measuring 4.5 x 1.4 cm in the axial plane.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. The visualized muscle bulk is intact.

Conclusion:
1. Radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No displaced meniscal fragments. 
2. No acute ligamentous injury, especially no tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
3. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild degenerative subchondral cystic changes and edema are present at the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau. Mild cystic changes are present at the tibial spines. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is a large, complex tear involving the anterior horn and body, extending to the posterior horn, with moderate extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Moderate to severe cartilage loss is present, most prominent at the posterior aspect. Small osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella diffusely. Moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring is present at the trochlea diffusely, with a chondral flap at the lateral trochlear facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is severe mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, with evidence of chronic partial tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Lateral meniscal tear with extrusion.
2. Chondrosis in the patellofemoral and lateral tibiofemoral compartment.
3. Severe mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament with evidence of chronic partial tear.
4. Moderate Baker cyst.

Interprétation :

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire. Liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité sans kyste de Baker significatif. 

Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont intacts sans déchirure.

Légère atténuation diffuse des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne sans atteinte transfixiante, en lien avec de légers changements dégénératifs/chondropathie. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Le ménisque externe de même que le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe sont intacts sans déchirure. Les surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe sont relativement préservées sans atteinte transfixiante.

Il y a une infiltration kystique ganglionnaire au sein du ligament croisé antérieur sans déchirure transfixiante. Également, petits kystes para-ligamentaires. Le ligament croisé postérieur est intact sans déchirure.

Il y a une patella alta. Il y a un foyer d’œdème au versant supéro-externe de la graisse de Hoffa en lien avec un syndrome de friction du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe. Légère tendinose du tendon patellaire sans déchirure.  Légère tendinose du tendon du quadriceps distal, sans déchirure.

Il y a une atténuation modérée des surfaces cartilagineuses au compartiment patellofémoral avec fissures chondrales de haut grade le long de la facette patellaire externe et de l’apex patellaire en lien avec des changements dégénératifs/chondropathie modérée. De plus, foyer de chondropathie focale sévère à la facette patellaire interne avec fissures chondrales transfixiantes et petit foyer de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ébauche d’ostéophytes marginaux.

Conclusion :

Il n’y a pas de dérangement interne (pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire significative).

Minime épanchement intra-articulaire.

Infiltration kystique ganglionnaire du ligament croisé antérieur sans déchirure transfixiante.

Changements dégénératifs/chondropathie légère au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et modérée au compartiment patellofémoral avec foyer de chondropathie sévère le long de la facette patellaire interne.

Patella alta. Signes d’un syndrome d’accrochage du tendon patellaire et du condyle fémoral externe (Hoffa’s fat pad impingement).

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Few day history of knee pain following skiing injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral tibial plateau. Low-grade osseous contusion along the posteromedial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate hemarthrosis. Disruption of the posterolateral joint capsule with edema tracking along the posterior knee interfascial planes. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear involving the body and posterior horn medial meniscus without extrusion or displaced fragment.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle towards the intercondylar notch.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade near full-thickness cartilage loss along the median ridge-medial patellar facet junction with overhanging edges. Trochlear cartilage remains intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete ACL tear with torn fibers along the anterior intercondylar notch.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain characterized by periligamentous edema without fiber disruption.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: There is low-grade partial-thickness tearing involving the distal conjoint tendon and partial tearing of the popliteofibular ligament.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Suspected partial tearing of the MPFL at the medial patellar attachment with superimposed disruption of the medial patellar retinaculum.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is marked lateral patellar translation and mild lateral patellar tilt. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complete ACL tear with associated osteochondral impaction injury of the posterolateral tibial plateau and osseous contusion at the posteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Lateral patellar subluxation possibly sequela of lateral patellar dislocation with partial disruption of the MPFL and medial patellar retinaculum. Additional near full-thickness focal cartilage defect at the median ridge and medial patellar facet possibly posttraumatic.
3.	Oblique undersurface tear posterior horn and body medial meniscus without displaced fragment or extrusion.
4.	Grade 1 sprain of the MCL.
5.	Grade 1 to low-grade 2 sprain of the distal conjoint tendon and popliteofibular ligament at the posterolateral corner. 
6.	Moderate hemarthrosis.
